questions.title: Idempotent APIs
questions.prompt: A client retries POST /payments after a timeout. How do you make sure the customer isn't charged twice?
expectedConcepts: Idempotency keys supplied by the client
Store the key with a unique constraint and the result
Return the stored response for duplicates
questions.answerOutline: The client generates a key per logical operation; the server atomically records it, processes once, stores the outcome, and replays the outcome on retries. Discuss the race between two simultaneous retries.
commonMistakes: Server-generated keys (the client can't reuse them)
Checking then inserting without a unique constraint
followUps: What if the downstream provider timed out?
How long do you keep keys?

questions.title: Exactly-once processing
questions.prompt: Your consumer reads order events from a queue and updates inventory. How do you avoid double-decrementing stock?
expectedConcepts: At-least-once delivery is the realistic default
Dedup table keyed by event ID in the same transaction
questions.answerOutline: Accept at-least-once delivery, make the effect idempotent by recording processed event IDs in the same DB transaction as the stock update, and use partition keys for ordering.
commonMistakes: Assuming the broker guarantees exactly-once end to end
followUps: How do you replay events safely?
questions.rubricNotes: Reward candidates who name the dual-write problem.
